title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
Tesla's Autopilot system was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family that data from the vehicle's systems recording what happened before the crash was unavailable. A security researcher later demonstrated that such data was routinely retained on Tesla vehicles, contradicting Tesla's claim to the family.

The failure was in information handling during a high-stakes situation where a family sought answers about their loss. Tesla had access to crash data but did not preserve it, disclose it, or correct its own statement to the family before the matter reached litigation. A manual review of data retention practices and a requirement to produce all available information in fatal crash cases would have caught this.

It is not established whether Tesla's initial claim to the family reflected a technical misunderstanding, a systems failure, or intentional withholding.
